OWNER FIX NEEDED (protected .github/workflows/research-agent.yml) — ALREADY TRACKED by OPEN issue #430: add `allowed_bots: "github-actions"` to the with: block of the claude-code-action@v1 step(s). The action's own error message states the remedy ('Add bot to allowed_bots list'). The value is normalized (lowercased, trailing [bot] stripped), so either `github-actions` or `github-actions[bot]` works. Scope to the one trusted first-party Actions bot and do NOT use `*` on this public repo (the action's docs warn `*` may let external Apps invoke it with attacker-controlled prompts). github-actions is the only actor able to dispatch this workflow (requires actions:write). The escalation only ever dispatches -f tier=deep, so the two deep steps (Fable 5 'deep, preferred' and Opus 4.8 'deep fallback') are load-bearing; adding it to the standard step too is harmless and keeps the three steps uniform. Safe because the research prompt is hardcoded in the workflow (not dispatcher-controlled) and `tier` is the only dispatch input, so this re-enables ONLY the recall fast-lane with no attacker-controlled-prompt vector.

Could NOT author the fix: this is the unattended Self-repair CI agent (GITHUB_ACTIONS=true, CI=true), so the CI-only scripts/hooks/protect-automation.js PreToolUse hook fires and BLOCKS any Edit/Write/Bash mutation of .github/workflows/** ('A human must author changes to these files'). Re-confirmed this run: on a self-repair/ branch the Edit adding allowed_bots to research-agent.yml was blocked by the hook (exit 2); branch deleted, working tree clean. By design an unattended CI agent cannot author protected-path (.github/workflows/**) changes — the hook is a hard safety invariant and was NOT circumvented (no env-var/API/indirect-write workaround attempted) — so no PR is possible and the fix must be applied by a human.

No non-protected fix exists: the breakage is the bot-actor gate on the dispatched run. Any GITHUB_TOKEN-authenticated `gh workflow run`/repository_dispatch produces a Bot actor regardless of event, so changing escalate-research.js cannot make the dispatch a human actor without a new PAT secret + workflow wiring (itself a protected change). The one-line allowed_bots addition is the correct, minimal fix.
